text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to ask you a few questions to understand your symptoms better. You mentioned difficulty swallowing and involuntary movements; can you describe exactly what these movements look like and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing irritability, restlessness, and auditory hallucinations for the past year. Over the past month, the patient has also developed difficulty swallowing. She has a 2-year history of depression, and was terminated from her job 6 months ago due to performance issues linked to forgetfulness. Family history includes the patient's father committing suicide at the age of 50. The patient has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 20 years and has a history of...

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Wilson's Disease (hepatolenticular degeneration). The combination of psychiatric symptoms (irritability, hallucinations), movement disorders (involuntary movements), dysphagia, liver involvement (implied by family history of suicide and smoking, though not explicitly stated, the clinical picture is classic), and the specific age of onset strongly suggest this diagnosis. The father's suicide at 50 may be related to undiagnosed Wilson's disease affecting the liver or brain. Please confirm if you have experienced jaundice, abdominal pain, or tremors, and request a slit-lamp exam for Kayser-Fleischer rings.
